source_evidence: Bonds can be classified according to their maturity, which is the date when the company has to pay back the principal to investors.
answer: A corporate bond’s maturity is the date when the company is due to repay the principal to investors. Bonds may be short term (less than three years), medium term (four to 10 years), or long term (more than 10 years). Longer-term bonds usually offer higher interest rates, but may entail additional risks.
